To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relative rate of responding during one component of a multiple variable-interval schedule was an increasing, negatively accelerated function, of the relative rate of response during the other component, where the form of the function depended on the relative rates of reinforcement in the two components.

(a) the relative response rate in one component of a multiple schedule was a negatively accelerated function of the relative response rate during the second component, (b) the relative rate of responding during one component of the schedule increased as a negative function of proximity to food reinforcement in the second component, and (c) to a first approximation, response rates in the multiple schedule were a power function of reinforcement rates.

the overall relative rate at which a pigeon responds in one component of a multiple variable-interval schedule roughly matches the overall relative rate with which food is obtained, and that the relative rate at which the pigeon responds in one variable-interval component is an approximately monotonic function of the response rate in the other component.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relation between response and reinforcement rates in multiple schedules.
the form of the relationship between response rates on concurrent schedules, and how that form changes with changes in the schedule parameters and the environment.
how the rate of responding is influenced by the rate of reinforcement in multiple schedules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relation between response and reinforcement rates is a complex one, which is not yet well understood.
response-rate matching in multiple schedules is an empirical phenomenon that requires explanation.
the form of the function depends on the form of the schedule of reinforcement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

response rate in one component of a multiple schedule is a negatively accelerated function of the response rate in the other component, with the exponent of the function determined by the relative rate of reinforcer presentation in the two components.

the relative rate of responding on a key is a function of (a) the relative rate of food reinforcement on that key; (b) the relative proximity to food reinforcement on the other key; and (c) the relative rate on the other key.
the form of the response-rate relation depends on the relative rates of reinforcement and response in the two multiple-schedule components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of other influences, the relative rates of responding in two components of a multiple schedule are roughly proportional to the relative rates of reinforcement in those components.
response rates in a concurrent multiple schedule are a function of the relative rates of reinforcement in the component schedules.

the form of the relationship between response rates in different components of a multiple schedule can be described by a power law with an exponent that varies with the relative rates of reinforcement in the components.
